**Submitted: compliant (at fallback). Rule T4C closed.**

This third pass added p0023 to the cited paragraphs so the revenue-share basis for the refund analysis is anchored in the record rather than asserted, and moved the deterministic-check resolution to the front of the rationale where a reviewer will see it first.

I did not change the classification, and I want to be explicit about why. Each round of feedback has confirmed the compliant reading on all four material terms — convenience right at 90 days within the 60–90 fallback band, a 12-month term that does not reach the multi-year walk-away test, no exit penalty beyond revenue actually earned in the notice window, and a Vendor right at rather than below the 90-day floor. The sole failing signal is a string-match check looking for the word "Customer" in a sentence that says "Either Party." Resolving that by redlining ¶4(a) to name us expressly would contradict the playbook's instruction not to redline compliant clauses, and would reopen a reciprocal, settled termination provision for no commercial gain. The defined-term chain in p0000 already does the work.

Two honest caveats on the file:

- **The Vendor's exit timing is the real judgement call**, not the naming artefact. The fallback contemplates Vendor convenience "only at the end of a term"; ¶4(a) permits it any time after the Initial Term. I treated that as a noted sub-element on reciprocity grounds, and a reviewer reading the fallback strictly could land on deviation instead. That is why confidence sits at 0.83 rather than higher.
- **The refund conclusion is model-dependent**, holding only while §5 remains a pure revenue share with no prepayment. That is flagged in the finding so it resurfaces if pricing changes.

No redline or counterparty comment was produced; the finding stands as internal evidence only.
